items.event_time_ist: NHC Advisory 22 issued 2:00 PM PDT (2:30 AM IST, Oct 13), Oct 12
items.summary: NHC Advisory 22 (2 PM MST Oct 12) lowered Simon's maximum sustained winds to 100 mph (still Category 2), centered about 75 miles W of Cabo Corrientes and about 210 miles S of Mazatlan, moving west-northwest at 3 mph with a minimum central pressure of 969 mb. Mexico discontinued the Tropical Storm Warning from Playa Perula to Cabo Corrientes; a hurricane warning remains in effect only for Las Islas Marias, with a hurricane watch from Cabo Corrientes to Bahia Tempehuaya. Forecast: near Las Islas Marias tonight into Tuesday, then approaching the west-central Mexico coast Wednesday into Thursday; NHC says Simon could re-intensify somewhat by Wednesday and remain a hurricane through midweek, with rapid weakening after it moves inland late in the week. Rainfall: 5-10 inches across coastal west-central Mexico with isolated maximums of 15 inches over Sinaloa by Thursday; a dangerous storm surge is possible along the immediate coast near Las Islas Marias.
items.title: Simon down to 100 mph in NHC Advisory 22; coastal warnings trimmed again

items.event_time_ist: Jalisco civil protection briefing held morning of Oct 12 (aired ~11:15 AM PDT / 11:45 PM IST, Oct 12)
items.source_name: Jalisco civil protection briefing (via Jalisco Noticias)
items.summary: Jalisco's civil protection briefing Monday outlined the Simon response so far: roughly 14,000 people evacuated, about 8,500 tourists kept safely in hotels, and just over 800 people remaining in shelters. Starting Tuesday, Oct 13, non-essential preventive measures are being lifted: in-person school classes resume and tourism and private-supply businesses can gradually reopen stores and shopping centers; public transit is resuming, though government administrative offices stay closed pending infrastructure evaluations. Officials reported significant storm-surge damage in Cihuatlan and La Huerta, a river overflow affecting Colima, and a pending agricultural-damage assessment in Tomatlan; no wind damage was reported, though 3-4 meter swells are still expected through Wednesday. Azteca ADN40 field reports separately put Puerto Vallarta/Nayarit affected homes above 3,000.
items.title: Jalisco briefing: ~14,000 evacuated, schools resume Tuesday Oct 13; storm surge damage in Cihuatlan/La Huerta
